verdict.winner: EPDM rubber roofing wins on charted lifespan and cold-weather seam simplicity; TPO wins on reflective cool-roof performance.
verdict.reasoning: Choose EPDM rubber roofing over TPO when the flat roof prioritizes charted longevity and field-repairable seams — EPDM lasts 15-25 years on the InterNACHI chart versus TPO's 7-20, and its adhesive-and-tape seams patch without a hot-air welder, per InterNACHI and NRCA guidance.
verdict.alternate: Choose TPO over EPDM rubber roofing when summer cooling load leads — TPO's white membrane carries ~0.70-0.85 solar reflectance per ASTM C1549 (CRRC-listed) and a reflective roof stays over 50F cooler than a conventional roof on a sunny afternoon, per the U.S. Department of Energy.

keyFacts: EPDM rubber roofing lasts 15-25 years versus TPO's 7-20 years on the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, with TPO commonly cited at 15-25 years in field practice (InterNACHI; Progressive Materials).
EPDM rubber roofing installs at $7.00-$10.00 per square foot in NJ versus TPO at $8.00-$12.00 per square foot (Josten Roofing).
EPDM is black and absorbs solar heat; TPO is white and reflects solar heat (gold comparison table).
EPDM seams are joined with adhesive or seam tape; TPO seams are hot-air-welded (gold comparison table).
EPDM's primary failure mode is seam separation; TPO's primary failure mode is welded-seam breakdown (NRCA-attributed trade data).
EPDM's secondary failure modes are puncture, membrane shrinkage pulling the sheet from penetrations and perimeters, and ponding-water stretching (NRCA-attributed trade data).
TPO's secondary failure modes are chemical attack from rooftop grease and equipment and thermal-shock cracking as plasticizers migrate out and the sheet hardens (NRCA technical guidance).
TPO's white membrane carries ~0.70-0.85 solar reflectance, rated per ASTM C1549 and CRRC-listed (ASTM C1549; Cool Roof Rating Council).
A reflective (cool) roof stays over 50F cooler than a conventional roof on a sunny afternoon (U.S. Department of Energy).
A reflective roof cuts peak cooling demand 11-27% in air-conditioned buildings (EPA), with the caveat that Newark's heating-dominated Climate Zone 4A-5 carries a winter heating offset (DOE).
Cool-roof performance is rated by solar reflectance and thermal emittance by the Cool Roof Rating Council, not by R-value (Cool Roof Rating Council).
EPDM ships black because carbon black acts as its UV stabilizer, and black EPDM outlasts white EPDM; a white EPDM line exists but still uses adhesive seams (Firestone-attributed industry guidance).
Elastomeric white coatings can raise an EPDM roof's reflectance but reapply on a cycle (gold FAQ).
NJ flat-roof small-patch repair runs $300-$500 for EPDM (primer plus cover patch) versus $200-$500 for a TPO patch or weld (HomeGuide; Modernize).
A TPO seam re-weld reseals at $200-$400 rather than re-adhering; broader TPO flat-roof repair spans $2.50-$10.00 per square foot or $300-$1,100 (Josten Roofing; HomeGuide; Modernize).
A small residential EPDM flat-section minor-leak repair sits in the $150-$500 band (Angi).
EPDM repairs require no welder (clean, prime, apply cover patch); TPO repairs require hot-air-welding (Modernize; WeatherShield).
sources: NRCA (National Roofing Contractors Association) technical guidance / trade data
njContext: EPDM installs at $7.00-$10.00 per square foot in NJ and TPO at $8.00-$12.00 per square foot (Josten Roofing).

The NJ Uniform Construction Code treats a full EPDM or TPO re-roof on a detached 1- or 2-family dwelling as ordinary maintenance — no permit, inspection, or notice (N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7; NJ DCA 2018 alert).

The NJ UCC requires a permit once flat-roof work on a commercial, condo, or attached building exceeds 25% of roof area within a 12-month period, or turns structural by cutting load-bearing support (N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7(b) and 5:23-2.7(c)).

TPO reaches NJ cool-roof relevance through the NJ Clean Energy Program's reflective-roof framing, while EPDM meets the same NJ UCC acceptance without a reflective surface (N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7; NJ Clean Energy Program).
Newark sits in heating-dominated Climate Zone 4A-5, so TPO's summer cooling benefit carries a winter heating offset (DOE).
On Essex County homes, EPDM's black sheet suits low-visibility flat sections (porches, additions, garage roofs) inconspicuously, while TPO's white reflective sheet suits sun-exposed sections (DOE).

An existing EPDM commercial field simplifies a like-for-like EPDM re-cover, since adhesive-and-tape seams add to the existing membrane without the welder a full TPO conversion requires (NRCA installation guidance).
positioning: Position Newark Quality Roofing as a registered New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor (registration under N.J.S.A. 56:8-136), insured, offering a free written estimate for both EPDM and TPO flat-roof systems across Essex County. NQR installs and repairs either single-ply membrane and helps the building owner choose based on the verified decision factors (charted longevity and field-repairable seams favor EPDM; reflective cool-roof cooling-load reduction favors TPO). Frame any warranty honestly as a two-part structure — the manufacturer's material warranty plus NQR's written contractor workmanship warranty — never as manufacturer certification tiers or named installer-program credentials. NQR scopes NJ UCC permit needs honestly: a detached 1-2 family re-roof is ordinary maintenance, while commercial/attached work over 25% of roof area in 12 months requires a permit.

buyersGuide.h1: Which Is Better: Rubber Roofing vs TPO?
buyersGuide.directAnswerThesis: Neither wins outright: EPDM rubber roofing wins on charted lifespan (15-25 vs TPO's 7-20 years, InterNACHI) and welder-free seam repair; TPO wins when summer cooling load leads via its ~0.70-0.85 reflective white surface.
